title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
authors: Yalin E. Sagduyu; Tugba Erpek; Yi Shi
abstract: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

title: NLP-based Message Prioritisation for Opportunistic Routing: A Case Study of Nepal Earthquake Emergency Communication
authors: Yihang Cao; Milena Radenkovic
abstract: This dissertation investigates whether Natural Language Processing (NLP) based semantic message prioritisation can improve the treatment of urgent disaster messages in opportunistic emergency communication, using the 2015 Nepal earthquake as a case study. TF IDF with Logistic Regression and BERT are used to classify social media messages into nine humanitarian categories, which are mapped to four routing priorities from P1 to P4. These priorities are integrated into the ONE simulator within a controlled Kathmandu earthquake scenario using a modified Binary Spray and Wait router. BERT achieves higher priority accuracy and P1 recall than Logistic Regression, while reducing under prioritisation and severe priority errors. However, improved NLP performance does not produce uniform network gains. P1 delivery probability remains high and similar across routing conditions, and no consistent latency reduction is observed. The clearest difference appears under buffer pressure, where the BERT condition shows fewer observed ground truth P1 buffer losses than Logistic Regression. The results indicate that semantic prioritisation is most valuable when limited transmission and storage resources are contested, although it cannot overcome mobility and contact constraints in opportunistic networks.

title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
authors: Zhengxin Li; Chongzhen Tian; Hui Yuan; Hao Liu; Sam Kwong
abstract: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. First, we develop a Local and Global Semantics-based Hybrid Token Pruning (LGS-HTP) module to significantly reduce the visual token count. By decoupling foreground-background tokens and jointly selecting local and global semantics, LGS-HTP effectively reduces redundancy while preserving reasoning-critical tokens. Second, we introduce a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding (T-JSCC) module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels. By employing lightweight cascaded linear layers and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-adaptive mechanism, this module adapts to fluctuating channel conditions while maintaining minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and SQA3D datasets indicate the exceptional efficiency and robustness of our approach. Specifically, on ScanQA validation set, the LGS-HTP module could achieve 90% pruning ratio while incurring less than a 1% CIDEr loss. Building on this, the T-JSCC further compresses the tokens by 18 times, resulting in an overall 180 times data volume reduction for robust transmission, while saving 90% in computational complexity for LVLM deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC.

title: Factors Affecting a Curriculum Based on Citizenship Legal Literacy Education
authors: Kobra Gholizadeh Chennab; Shahram Ranjdoust
venue: International Journal of Education and Cognitive Sciences
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to identify the factors affecting a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education in order to improve the quality of civic education in Iran’s educational system. Methods and Materials: This applied and developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, the statistical population included experts in education, curriculum planning, social sciences, and citizenship rights. Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through 15 semi-structured interviews, which continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The qualitative data were analyzed using MaxQDA software through open, axial, and selective coding. The extracted themes were then organized to develop a conceptual structure for a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education. Findings: The inferential findings supported a multidimensional structure for citizenship legal literacy education. The analysis indicated that five key components formed the core of the proposed curriculum model: citizenship rights education, values and beliefs, practical empowerment, development of social interaction, and media and digital literacy education. These components represented interrelated knowledge-based, attitudinal, behavioral, and social indicators. The findings showed that emphasis on citizens’ rights and responsibilities, justice-oriented attitudes, dialogue skills, social participation, legal awareness, responsible media use, and digital literacy plays a decisive role in designing an effective curriculum for educating law-abiding and participatory citizens. Conclusion: The results suggest that citizenship legal literacy education in Iran requires a shift from the mere transmission of theoretical concepts toward a competency-based, participatory, and practice-oriented curriculum. Such a curriculum can contribute to strengthening civic awareness, promoting legal responsibility, enhancing social participation, supporting educational justice, and preparing students for active and responsible citizenship in contemporary society.

title: Intelligent clinical decision support system for intracranial aneurysm lesion-based detection using biomedical imaging data
authors: S. Praveena; V. B. Murali Krishna; Vijaya Krishna Sonthi; Devi Priya Gottumukkala; Chinmaya Ranjan Pattanaik; Naliniprava Behera; Kritika Bansal
abstract: Abstract An intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a type of cerebrovascular condition that occurs due to focal bulging or expansion in the wall of a cerebral artery, most frequently affecting the internal carotid artery. An IA is seemingly connected with conditions such as fibrous dysplasia, adult-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and coarctation of aorta. A ruptured brain aneurysm can result in a severe and life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage if not treated early, often leading to long-lasting neurological damage and a higher chance of death. However, the traditional diagnostic technique is time-consuming, and it necessitates a trained and skilled medical practitioner. Hence, building an automated model to help physicians precisely detect IA can reduce the clinicians’ burden. Recently, deep learning has gained significant interest in the domain of medical imaging as it automatically learns patterns and accurately detects several types of diseases, such as IAs. Therefore, this article introduces a Clinical Decision Support System for Intracranial Aneurysm Lesion-Based Detection (CDSS-IALD). The main purpose of this work is to develop a robust system that can automatically detect and identify intracranial aneurysms using medical imaging data to assist clinicians with treatment decisions. Initially, the proposed CDSS-IALD model pre-processes the input biomedical images using image normalization, noise reduction, contrast improvement, and skull stripping to refine image quality and consistency for subsequent analysis. Following that, a ConvNeXt hierarchical model is employed for feature extraction, which effectively extracts local details and global context from pre-processed images. Finally, these extracted representations are then forwarded to a spiking neural network, which performs accurate aneurysm detection and classification. To ensure the enhanced performance of the CDSS-IALD system, extensive experiments were conducted on the benchmark Intracranial Aneurysm Dataset. The experimental outcomes clearly demonstrate the betterment of the proposed CDSS-IALD system over the other approaches in detecting and localizing intracranial aneurysms from biomedical imaging.

title: White matter damage across frontal–subcortical circuits in carbon monoxide intoxication: Insights from fixel-based analysis
authors: Chiung‐Chih Chang; Jur-Shan Cheng; Hsin-I. Chang; Shih‐Wei Hsu; Chi-Wei Huang; Yao-Liang Chen; Jiun‐Jie Wang
abstract: Background Carbon monoxide intoxication (COI) can cause white matter damage through neurotoxic effects. This study investigated these abnormalities within frontal–subcortical circuits and their association with cognitive impairment. Methods 91 COI patients at chronic stage and 20 heathy controls were enrolled. Patients were divided into 3 severity groups (normal cognition; mild cognitive impairment, MCI; and dementia). Voxel-based morphometry and fixel-based analysis were evaluated between patients, as well as across different severity subgroups, and healthy controls. Regression analysis was conducted between the fixel derived metrics and the cognitive composite scores. Significance was set as family-wise error-corrected p < 0.05. Results White matter damage can be detected across frontal–subcortical circuits at chronic stage of CO intoxication. Compared with healthy controls, damage in COI patients with normal cognition can be found in the cingulum even without significant grey matter lesion. The COI-MCI group showed sporadically localized white matter abnormalities in motor, dorsolateral prefrontal and anterior cingulate circuits, whereas the COI-Dementia group demonstrated deficits involving multiple major white matter tracts, including the anterior limb of the internal capsule and anterior thalamic radiation, as well as basal ganglia, temporal and occipital lobes. Reduced fixel derived metrics in periventricular and frontal bundles, including the internal capsule, superior corona radiata and cingulum were highly correlated with cognitive performance in executive function (Pearson's r up to 0.674). Conclusions Damage in the frontal–subcortical circuits can be found in patients with carbon monoxide intoxication, which was correlated to the severity in the affected cognitive domains.

title: الروح في القرآن الكريم: دراسة استقرائية في الاستعمال والسياق والقراءات
authors: Khaled Borham
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: دراسة استقرائية في استعمالات اسم «الرُّوح» في القرآن الكريم وسياقاتها وقراءاتها. تعتمد الدراسة النص القرآني مرجعًا وتفحص التراكيب والضمائر والأفعال والسياق القريب ونظائر الآيات دون افتراض أن الاسم يدل على مرجع واحد أو ماهية واحدة.تفصل الدراسة بين الحصر الصرفي للجذر «ر و ح» وهو ٥٧ وقوعًا في ست صيغ وفق Quranic Arabic Corpus وبين التحليل الدلالي لاسم «رُوح» وهو ٢١ وقوعًا في ٢٠ آية. وتصف النتائج بدرجات هي الصريحة أو الراجحة أو المحتملة أو المسكوت عنها. وتتناول مواضع النفخ والإحياء والتنزيل والأمر والإيحاء والتأييد واقتران الروح بالملائكة وأثر القراءات في الوظيفة النحوية والإسراء ١٧: ٨٥ في سياقها القريب. ويُستعمل الطبري لتوثيق نقل أوجه القراءة فقط.ويرافق البحث مصنف Excel بعنوان «تحليل الجذر روح ٥٧ وقوع» يضم صفًا لكل وقوع وأوراقًا للتوزيع الصرفي والدلالي وحسب السور والمنهج والمصادر. EnglishAn inductive study of the uses of the noun al-rūḥ in the Noble Qur'an, its contexts and its variant readings. The study takes the Qur'anic text as its reference and examines constructions, pronouns, verbs, the immediate context and parallel verses, without assuming that the noun denotes a single referent or essence.It separates the morphological count of the root r-w-ḥ (57 occurrences in six forms according to the Quranic Arabic Corpus) from the semantic analysis of the noun rūḥ (21 occurrences in 20 verses). Its conclusions are graded as explicit, probable, possible or left unstated by the text. The study treats the passages on blowing and giving life, revelation, command, inspiration, support, the association of the rūḥ with the angels, the effect of variant readings on grammatical function, and al-Isrā' 17:85 in its immediate context. Al-Ṭabarī is used only to document the transmission of variant readings.The paper is accompanied by an Excel workbook, "تحليل الجذر روح 57 وقوع", with a row for each occurrence and sheets for the morphological, semantic and per-surah distributions and for method and sources.

title: Enterprise Informatics Capability and Manufacturing Supply Chain Resilience in the Digital Economy: The Roles of Information Transparency and Environmental Dynamism
venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
abstract: This study examines how enterprise informatics capability influences manufacturing supply chain resilience in the context of the digital economy.Drawing on organizational information processing theory and contingency theory, a moderated mediation model is developed to investigate the mediating role of information transparency and the moderating role of environmental dynamism.Survey data collected from 316 supply chain managers and senior executives in Chinese manufacturing firms are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.The findings indicate that enterprise informatics capability has a significant positive effect on manufacturing supply chain resilience both directly and indirectly through information transparency.Information transparency partially mediates this relationship by serving as a key information-transmission mechanism.Environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the direct effect of enterprise informatics capability on supply chain resilience; however, it positively moderates the indirect effect through information transparency, such that the mediating pathway becomes stronger in highly dynamic environments.The findings contribute to the enterprise informatics literature by clarifying the information-processing pathways through which informatics capability translates into supply chain resilience, and by identifying the boundary conditions under which these pathways operate.Practical implications for manufacturing managers seeking to strengthen supply chain resilience through informatics investment are discussed.

title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
authors: Paulius Skaisgiris; Thomas Pammer; Veronika Semmelrock; Mykyta Ielanskyi; Maximilian Heisinger; Erich Kobler
abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation has substantially improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, including code generation, data analysis, and exam-style question answering. Despite these advances, purely neural LLMs continue to struggle with elementary logical reasoning problems and lack the determinism, soundness, and reliability characteristic of symbolic reasoning systems. Conversely, classical symbolic methods such as SAT solving and exact cover guarantee correctness and completeness, but require problems to be expressed in highly specialized formal encodings, limiting their applicability to natural language inputs. In this work, we present a synergistic neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by combining neural semantic parsing with deterministic exact cover reasoning. Given a Zebra-style logic puzzle in natural language, an LLM translates entities and constraints into structured tool calls that construct an exact cover instance. A symbolic solver then computes the solution and provides feedback to iteratively refine invalid, under- or overconstrained encodings, exploiting the uniqueness property of Zebra puzzles. We conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple parameter scales, post-training paradigms, and LLM families. The results demonstrate that our hybrid approach consistently outperforms strong plain neural baselines, including CoT prompting, as well as recent neuro-symbolic methods.

title: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization
authors: Zitong Wang; Shuchang Lyu; Meng Li; Qiang Wang; Guangliang Cheng; Zhenwei Shi
abstract: Source-only domain generalization (DG) for remote sensing semantic segmentation seeks reliable predictions in unseen domains without target-domain data during training. Although vision foundation models offer transferable knowledge, category recognition remains sensitive to source-specific visual cues, while task-specific adaptation may weaken pretrained transferability. We propose ASCoR, an asymmetric semantic-spatial framework built on SAM3. Its text-conditioned semantic branch uses class-name prompts to provide explicit category guidance. Probe-Once Dynamic Adaptive LoRA distributes a fixed adaptation budget across encoder blocks to limit source-specific specialization. A complementary task-specific dense branch learns multi-scale spatial representations using a separate frozen SAM3 image encoder. A lightweight reliability router integrates the two branches through bounded spatial correction based on local prediction reliability. All components are trained using source-domain supervision only. Experiments on the ISPRS, LoveDA, and OpenEarthMap benchmarks cover nine cross-domain transfers. ASCoR achieves a state-of-the-art mean IoU of 68.61% across six ISPRS transfers, outperforming the previous best method by 2.69 percentage points. It also achieves the best results on all three LoveDA/OpenEarthMap transfers, with 59.07%, 47.95%, and 49.38% mIoU on Rural-to-Urban, Urban-to-Rural, and Urban-to-OpenEarthMap, respectively. Ablation studies, feature visualizations, and spatial reliability analyses support the effectiveness and complementarity of the proposed components. Code: https://github.com/WangZitong42/ASCoR.

title: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Dual-Granularity Contrastive Alignment for Preoperative Prediction of Lung Adenocarcinoma Invasiveness Using 3D CT
authors: Qing Huang; Xiaotong Tan; Lintong Yao; Wufeng Xue; Ruobing Huang; Dong Ni; Hao Wu; Tian Xiao; Jun Cheng
abstract: Accurate preoperative prediction of lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness is important for surgical planning and individualized treatment. However, overlapping CT appearances make it challenging to distinguish invasive adenocarcinoma (IAD) from Pre-IAD lesions. We propose a multimodal prompt-learning framework with dual-granularity image-text alignment for 3D CT-based IAD classification. A 3D ResNet-CBAM encoder extracts global and spatial visual features. A frozen RadBERT backbone is adapted with separate learnable prompts for report-level and keyword-level text encoding. These prompts are initialized using semantic representations derived from real-world clinical reports. Global contrastive alignment connects whole-volume CT representations with reports generated from clinician-annotated radiological attributes to provide overall semantic supervision. A multiple instance learning-based local alignment module associates spatial CT features with vascular-focused radiological keywords, to capture local imaging characteristics potentially associated with tumor invasion. The framework jointly optimizes classification and alignment objectives, while inference requires only CT images. Experiments included 1,593 pathologically confirmed nodules. On the test set, the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 87.92%, F1-score of 87.78%, and AUC of 0.9499. Its AUC significantly exceeded that of the image-only Res-CBAM baseline with the same visual backbone (0.9297; DeLong test, p = 0.0078). Ablation analyses supported the complementary contributions of global and local alignment and the benefit of report-based prompt initialization. Qualitative visualizations showed activation within nodules and adjacent vascular structures. These findings suggest that dual-granularity radiological supervision can enhance CT-based invasiveness prediction while preserving a CT-only inference workflow.

title: PACERec: Progressive Adaptation of LLM Item Embeddings with Collaborative Evidence for Recommendation
authors: Junzhao Huang; Xi Wu; Zihan Wang; Zijing Wang; Ming Wang; Kang Liu; Xiaocui Yang; Shi Feng; Daling Wang; Yifei Zhang; Ting Yang; Xurui Li
abstract: Large language model (LLM) embeddings have been increasingly adopted in sequential recommendation to encode static item attributes and alleviate the limitations of item ID embeddings under sparse interactions. However, these embeddings typically capture only static content similarity while neglecting sequential transitions, and since their adaptation quality relies on sparse per-item updates or global geometric calibration, existing methods still struggle to explicitly transfer preceding interaction contexts from frequent to long-tail items under unevenly distributed behavioral evidence, limiting recommendation effectiveness across the catalog. To address this challenge, we propose PACERec, an ID-free progressive adaptation framework that incorporates preceding interaction contexts into semantic representation adaptation by learning a shared velocity field from items with sufficient interactions via frequency-weighted flow matching. In this way, PACERec progressively guides static LLM embeddings toward collaborative behavioral targets while preserving original item semantics, overcoming sparse per-item updates to effectively generalize sequential transition patterns to long-tail items for both user modeling and candidate scoring. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets across three sequential backbones demonstrate the superiority of our method over competitive baselines in both overall and long-tail recommendation.

title: Balancing Representations by Identifying and Generating Under-represented Data
authors: Filipe Laitenberger; Hirokatsu Kataoka; Yuki Asano; Cees Snoek; Mohammadreza Salehi
abstract: Self-supervised learning inherits the coverage of its source data. When an unlabeled corpus is long-tailed, the representation becomes dense around frequent modes and thin where coverage is weak. Objectives for long-tailed SSL reweight the images already in the corpus and add no new ones. We introduce BRIDGE (Balancing Representations by Identifying and Generating Under-represented Data), a label-free feedback loop around the source set. The current encoder scores every source image by its mean kNN distance, and a budgeted acquisition rule selects images from a band of that score distribution where support is thin and the generator still produces faithful variants. A frozen image-to-image diffusion model then adds local variants of the selected anchors, and pretraining continues on the enlarged source set. We formulate acquisition as recoverability-weighted allocation of local support and derive when a finite budget should favor a sparse band that excludes the extreme tail and when reallocation after each repair is optimal under a fixed objective. Across five long-tailed, web-scraped and synthetic source regimes, BRIDGE has the highest seven-task linear-probe and kNN average of the compared methods, and paired experiments extend the gain to ViT-S under contrastive and self-distillation objectives, to low-label fine-tuning and to semantic segmentation. The linear-probe gain is smaller under masked reconstruction. Generated repair matches an oracle that restores the withheld real images, and under a frozen encoder the inserted images shrink the neighborhoods of the selected anchors about twice as much as those of matched unselected images. BRIDGE needs no labels and leaves the pretraining objective unchanged, so it can be added to pretraining on uncurated web data, where the encoder decides which images to generate.

title: RouteREPA: Routed Representation Alignment for Just Image Transformers
authors: Yi Tan; Beier Zhu; Sirui Chen; Cheng Chen; Xingyu Zhu; Yuan Zhou; Zhenshan Tan; Tianrun Chen; Hanwang Zhang
abstract: Representation alignment (REPA) is widely used to accelerate the training of latent-space diffusion transformers (DiTs). However, applying it to pixel-space models such as Just Image Transformers (JiT) is challenging. Our analysis reveals a pronounced representation conflict between discriminative alignment and pixel-space generation. Compared with its latent counterpart, JiT learns representations that are substantially less aligned with DINOv2. Applying REPA to JiT consistently reduces the reconstructability of its intermediate representations, whereas this effect is not observed in Latent JiT. We attribute this conflict to JiT directly reconstructing pixels, which requires its representations to hierarchically encode discriminative semantics and reconstruction-relevant visual information across network depths. To address these challenges, we propose Routed Representation Alignment (RouteREPA), which uses lightweight, representation-dependent routers to adaptively route task-oriented representations for alignment and generation. We further apply routing across multiple network depths to accommodate their depth-dependent representation requirements. Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K at 256x256 resolution show that RouteREPA consistently improves JiT across model scales and training budgets, outperforming standard REPA. On JiT-H/16, RouteREPA further surpasses PixelREPA using only one-third of its training epochs without classifier-free guidance.

title: SomaAlign: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Representation Learning for Soft Robotic Grasping
authors: Haoyuan Wang; Shuai Peng; Yongkai Liao; Yuxiao Sun; Wei Luo; Xinxing Chen; Jian Huang
abstract: Robust multimodal perception for soft robotic grasping is challenged by modality-dependent noise, semantic ambiguity, and limited coordinated multisensory data. We introduce Soma, a dataset containing 100 objects, 1,000 continuous grasping trajectories, and 74,914 multimodal samples grouped by software acquisition cycle, spanning remote RGB, hand RGB, depth, tactile, IMU, and structured text observations. We also collect Soma-Success, an independent grasp-outcome dataset with 1,000 trials (998 retained after quality control), to evaluate frozen-encoder transfer for post-hoc grasp outcome classification and early grasp success prediction. Built on Soma, SomaAlign learns multimodal representations in three stages: masked reconstruction estimates relative modality reliability; reliability-aware contrastive alignment uses pair-specific adaptive temperatures to adjust alignment sharpness; and conflict-aware semantic constraints improve intra-sample cross-modal consistency while preserving global feature geometry. SomaAlign achieves an average Recall@10 of 90.66% across 30 directed cross-modal retrieval tasks. The learned representations also support physical attribute recognition, multimodal question answering, cross-modal generation, and cross-dataset transfer to grasp outcome prediction. On Soma-Success, frozen SomaAlign encoders with lightweight probes achieve 94.59% post-hoc classification accuracy and 84.07% early prediction accuracy. Together, Soma, Soma-Success, and SomaAlign provide a data and representation-learning foundation for robust and transferable multimodal perception in soft robotic manipulation.

title: Discovering Semantic Granularity in Images through Clustering of Pretrained Visual Representations
authors: Ying Dai
abstract: Semantic granularity, which refers to the levels at which visual representations organize image content into meaningful entities, is fundamental to image understanding. However, whether pretrained visual representations inherently encode semantic structures at multiple granularities remains poorly understood. This paper presents a representation-driven approach for discovering semantically meaningful image regions at different granularities through clustering of pretrained visual representations without semantic supervision. Specifically, we concatenate selected feature maps extracted from a pretrained visual model and apply a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based projection to derive pixel-wise principal representation maps (PRMs). The resulting PRMs capture implicit semantic structures embedded in pretrained visual representations, making them accessible to subsequent semantic clustering. We then introduce the semantic continuity rate (SCR), based on the silhouette principle, to quantify the coherence of pixel-wise representations within and between clusters at different candidate granularities. Furthermore, we analyze the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of SCR profiles to assess representation suitability for discovering semantic regions at multiple granularities. Our results indicate that PRMs exhibiting higher SNR values over an initial range of cluster numbers tend to yield more semantically meaningful regions across multiple granularities. We evaluate the proposed approach on the COCO-2017 and VOC-2012 validation datasets using Hungarian-matched intersection over union (HIoU). The results demonstrate competitive segmentation performance among the compared methods, supporting the feasibility of discovering useful semantic granularities through clustering PRMs without semantic supervision.

title: SCARF: A Scene-Adaptive Depth-Guided G-3DGS Encoder Accelerator with Semantic Reuse and Fused Dataflow
authors: Zirui Ma; Zhihua Fan; Haibin Wu; Wenxing Li; Fulin Zhang; Dongrui Fan; Xiaochun Ye; Wenming Li
abstract: Depth-guided, cost-volume-based Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (G-3DGS) encoders reconstruct scenes as sets of Gaussian primitives directly from multi-view images without requiring per-scene optimization, thereby facilitating feed-forward novel-view synthesis on edge computing platforms. However, their shared encoder architecture presents two primary bottlenecks. First, the per-pixel depth search disregards semantic similarity within the 2D feature space, causing depth search operations to account for over 65% of memory traffic due to redundant exhaustive candidate scans. Second, the sequential pipeline of depth prediction followed by Gaussian generation neglects local 3D geometric continuity, resulting in more than 52% of generated Gaussians being redundant prior to instantiation. In this paper, we introduce SCARF, a dataflow-co-designed accelerator that aligns each bottleneck with a corresponding scene-level regularity. To mitigate the first bottleneck, Feature Similarity Depth Reuse reconceptualizes depth search as a problem of semantic locality: depth consistency is determined by affinity in feature space rather than physical address proximity. It transforms exhaustive per-pixel depth searches into anchor-centered local searches. To overcome the second bottleneck, Scene-Adaptive Early Sparsification disrupts the conventional serial depth-to-materialization boundary by probing each tile to infer local scene regularity. It then selectively activates only the minimally sufficient generation pathway, eliminating redundant Gaussian computations before primitive instantiation. On a 27.8 square millimeter 28 nm post-layout design, SCARF delivers a 2.94x geometric-mean end-to-end speedup with maximum PSNR degradation below 0.072%, 2.23 inferences per joule, and 34.5x GPU energy efficiency.

title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
authors: Takuro Shimaya; Junya Inoh; Masahiro Saiko
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) provides diverse patient information and various clinical tasks, for which numerous deep learning models have been investigated. Recent years have seen the development of vision-language foundation models that can comprehensively extract clinical features, driven by representation learning that combines CT volumes with radiology reports. Existing approaches typically adopt Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP)-based representation learning, where pairs from different cases are, in principle, treated as negative pairs such that the volume and report embeddings are pushed apart. In the biomedical imaging, however, treating different cases as negative pairs is not always appropriate, particularly when clinical similarity exists. In this study, we propose a supervised representation learning framework grounded in clinical knowledge from language foundation models, rather than the weak supervision used in CLIP. Specifically, we utilized a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from reports. We then explicitly constructed the target features that the image encoder should output, as the semantic representation of the extracted findings using a biomedical text embedding model. Our Findings-aware Language-Image Pre-training (FiLIP) outperformed weakly supervised approaches in multi-label zero-shot finding classification in both in-domain and external-domain evaluations, and also proved effective when fine-tuned for the downstream task of radiology report generation.

title: Beyond Faces: Toward Interactive Generative Video Coding via Hybrid Priors
authors: Jianhui Chang; Jialei Zhou; Giuseppe Valenzise; 灏烨 张; Lihu Xiao; Siwei Ma
abstract: Generative face video coding (GFVC) is effective for ultra-lowbitrate talking-head communication, but practical video conferencing often involves hand gestures and face-hand occlusions that are not well handled by existing face-centric pipelines. In such hand-active scenarios, facial and hand motion follow heterogeneous dynamics that complicate compact representation, motion transformation, and reconstruction. To address this, we present a hybrid-prior framework for interactive generative video coding. Our method combines a semantically disentangled structural prior, encoded by compact face-hand landmarks for motion alignment and pose guidance, with a pretrained generative prior, instantiated by a conditional latent diffusion decoder for reconstructing newly emerged or heavily occluded content. Concretely, we introduce a motion-factorized alignment module that decouples facial and hand motion, and a diffusion-based reconstruction stage conditioned on both pose maps and motion-transferred features. We further construct a hand-active benchmark tailored to interactive video conferencing. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction quality and compression performance over VVC and representative GFVC baselines on both full-frame and hand-region metrics. In particular, it achieves bitrate savings of 60.6% and 76.1% over VVC in terms of LPIPS and DISTS, while also yielding clear improvements in hand-sensitive regions.

title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
authors: Muhammad Ahsan Hayat; Jahangir Baig; Shayan Ahmed; Ahmed Faraz Ayubi
abstract: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: Retrieval-Assisted Scalar Grounding for Natural-Language Optimization: A Diagnostic Study
authors: Soroush Vahidi
abstract: Abstract Retrieval and structural checks can make natural-language optimization outputs appear usable even when numerical grounding—assigning textual quantities to model parameters—is incomplete. We examine this diagnostic gap through three questions: fixed-catalog schema identification, the validity of coverage/type readiness as a numerical check, and the mechanisms underlying grounding outcomes. On 331 queries from NLP4LP, a benchmark for natural-language linear and mixed-integer linear programming, and 335 schema documents, term frequency–inverse document frequency retrieval and a pretrained dense encoder identify the target schema for 301 and 313 queries. Lexical grounding with multiplicative-word extraction passes coverage/type readiness on 265 queries, but only seven meet the complete stored-reference scalar-tolerance criterion: 2.64% of ready outputs. A mutually exclusive residual partition distinguishes retrieval, coverage, type, and numerical failures. Six grounding procedures under fixed retrieval yield between seven and 46 complete successes, with candidates, scoring, abstention, and decoding changing together. A separate 49-query assignment study with fixed candidates and scores improves exact slot counts without increasing the five whole-instance tolerance successes, limiting attribution to search. The methodological contribution is joint reporting of retrieval, readiness, and complete scalar agreement with explicit assistance, denominators, and evidence boundaries. Reference-derived inventories and benchmark exposure restrict the findings to assisted grounding. Supplementary relationship judgments and author contrasts assisted by artificial intelligence illustrate semantic limits without establishing accuracy. A versioned public release supports saved-record reanalysis; missing historical predictions and restricted originals prevent full experimental reproduction.

title: A Domain-Intelligent Multi-Agent AI Framework for Upstream Subsurface Data Querying
authors: J. P. Soares; A. Thompson; Nagaraju Reddicharla; S. Ghosh; M. Sharma; A. Nikulchev; V. Haiduk; D. Belov
venue: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope In upstream operations, professionals must make rapid decisions, yet critical data is often fragmented across complex schemas, causing delays or errors. This paper presents a GPT-5-based multi-agent AI framework that enables engineers to query enterprise data in natural language and receive validated, contextualized answers with supporting evidence in under one minute. The objective is to reduce decision latency and improve reliability in subsurface workflows by providing consistent, accurate, and immediately actionable data access. Methods, Procedures, Process The framework operates through four agents. The Domain Intelligence Agent (DIA) contextualizes queries using operator-specific naming conventions, business rules, and schema relationships, enabling accurate schema linking. Retrieval follows a two-stage approach: semantic table selection, then column refinement. Controlled experiments (N>300) showed table-first retrieval significantly improves SQL quality (p=0.031) versus column-level indexing. A SQL agent generates and self-corrects queries with validation against schema constraints and join paths. Finally, dual verification agents assess schema consistency, semantic correctness, and the plausibility of the generated results, ensuring output reliability before returning validated outputs or reports. Results, Observations, Conclusions The framework achieved >85% execution accuracy across 300 subsurface queries spanning 50+ tables. Accuracy is defined as successful execution producing semantically correct results, validated through Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based comparison, LLM-as-judge scoring, and SME review. These complementary methods capture distinct failure modes. Error analysis shows primary failure drivers include ambiguous queries (21% of incorrect outputs), database inconsistencies (17%), complex join-path errors (9%), and aggregation or unit misinterpretation (6%). Notably, over 30% of initially incorrect outputs were reclassified as external issues (prompt ambiguity or data quality), suggesting a lower intrinsic model error rate. A subsequent two-week field validation, in which 40 practicing SMEs posed more than 700 of their own daily-work questions and rated responses against a formal correctness rubric, corroborated this result with an independently assessed accuracy exceeding 93%. Standard benchmarks such as Spider and BIRD were not directly applied due to limited alignment with upstream schema complexity. Instead, a domain-specific benchmark dataset was developed, reflecting realistic subsurface workflows. Operationally, the system reduces reliance on manual data extraction, enabling users to obtain validated answers within minutes. Early adoption shows improved efficiency and a shift from reactive reporting to proactive data exploration. The framework has been validated through internal pilots, live demonstrations, and use in real operational tasks. Novel/Additive Information This work introduces a portable Domain Intelligence Agent that encodes domain knowledge for scalable deployment. It demonstrates, with statistical evidence (p=0.031), that table-first retrieval improves NL-to-SQL performance in complex industrial schemas with overlapping semantics. The study also proposes an error-aware evaluation framework that separates model performance from data and ambiguity issues. By enabling reliable data access at scale, the framework provides a foundation for future upstream AI agents and autonomous analytical workflows.

title: Association of Regular Yoga Practice with Metabolic and Physiological Health in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: B Guhacharan; K Bhagyalakshmi; Arun Kumar Nayanatara; N Anupama; B Shetty Sneha; Sathish B Rao
abstract: Purpose: The present study aimed to examine whether regular yoga practice is associated with differences in metabolic, cardiopulmonary, cognitive, and psychological health among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study included 236 adults with T2DM, comprising 79 regular yoga practitioners and 157 non-practitioners. Anthropometric measurements, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, blood pressure, peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR), heart rate variability (HRV), Diabetic Neuropathy Score (DNS), Letter Cancellation Test (LCT), and Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21) scores were assessed using standardized procedures. Data were analyzed using the unpaired Student's t-test and Chi-square test, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Compared with non-practitioners, participants practicing yoga demonstrated significantly lower fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, diabetic neuropathy scores, anxiety, and stress levels (P < 0.05). They also demonstrated better cognitive performance on the Letter Cancellation Test (P = 0.041). Conclusions: Regular yoga practice was associated with better metabolic control, selected cardiopulmonary parameters, cognitive performance, and psychological well-being among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. These findings suggest a potential role for yoga as a complementary lifestyle practice; however, prospective randomized controlled studies are required to establish causality.

title: Flat Features, Detailed Images? Simple Detail Control for Diffusion Transformers
authors: Qingtao Yu; Zhen Wang; Jiyang Zheng; Minghao Sun; Hongdong Li; Dylan Campbell
abstract: Prompt engineering is commonly used to encourage text-to-image models to generate more detailed images. However, it does not provide reliable, continuous, or disentangled control. We analyze feature tokens produced with and without detail-enhancing prompts across six diffusion transformers and observe a common pattern: these prompts tend to increase the entropy of each token's energy distribution while largely preserving its ordering. That is, flattening the distribution increases the level of detail. Motivated by this counter-intuitive finding, we introduce a simple training-free approach that continuously adjusts the level of detail according to a scalar. Specifically, it shifts the squared channel magnitudes of each token toward a higher entropy distribution with a time-aware scheduler to concentrate the intervention at intermediate sampling steps. Across extensive experiments on different types of diffusion transformers, we show that our approach provides continuous control over detail metrics while largely preserving image quality and semantic structure. It requires only a few lines of code and adds negligible inference time overhead.

title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
authors: Haoqing Wang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Sicheng Fan; Zhexin Zhang; Xinjie Zhang; Jiahao Li; Bin Li; Yan Lu
abstract: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle tasks ranging from everyday desktop activities to long-horizon professional workflows. Yet interfaces centered on screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions can impose a human-interaction prior, requiring repeated screen interpretation while leaving the computer's semantic and programmatic capabilities underexposed. We argue for exposing these capabilities and letting models choose and combine them. We introduce Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), a unified interface for general agents that combines three complementary channels: programmatic interaction through code and command-line tools, semantic interaction through accessibility (AX), and visual interaction through graphical user interfaces (GUI). Our HCU supports efficient AX interaction and guards against stale-state actions during channel switching. A supplementary HCU skill guides agents in selecting and coordinating channels to use the unified interface effectively. Our designed AX tools return compact observations, execute actions in batches, and report their effects as AX diffs, so the model needs fewer round trips. On OSWorld 2.0, HCU achieves the highest Partial and Binary scores among the compared systems. Analyzing agent trajectories, we find that all evaluated models improve with HCU yet allocate work across the channels differently and consistently outperform compared baselines in terms of both efficiency and task success, highlighting the value of unified computer-use interfaces that allow flexible channel selection and combination.

title: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version)
authors: Jens Sprengers; Marton Bognar; Lesly-Ann Daniel; Frank Piessens
abstract: Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a microarchitectural optimization recently introduced in mainstream desktop and server CPUs. Although DMPs offer performance improvements, they have been shown to enable side-channel leakage of secrets, even from constant-time code that has been hardened against Spectre attacks. Unfortunately, existing defenses either incur significant performance overhead or, as we show, fail to prevent all DMP leakage. In this work, we address this gap by designing a defense that is both secure and efficient. First, we propose a classification of DMP leakage, categorize existing and novel attacks, and analyze which leakage classes are mitigated by existing defenses. We validate this analysis empirically by implementing the first open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor, showing that the only existing defense that aims to preserve DMP performance fails to protect against entire leakage classes. Next, we propose SecDMP, a provably secure and efficient hardware-based defense. SecDMP requires secrets to be marked in memory and ensures that DMPs never encode these secrets in the microarchitecture---without compromising performance for public data. We formally prove that SecDMP introduces no leakage beyond a baseline semantics without DMPs. Notably, when combined with speculative-execution defenses, SecDMP restores complete microarchitectural security for constant-time code. Finally, our empirical evaluation shows that SecDMP prevents all DMP leakage while incurring minimal performance overhead and hardware cost.

title: Semantic Transferability of Generative Rate-Distortion-Perception Systems
authors: Jinwan Jeon; Seoyeon Hwang; Sung Hoon Lim
abstract: Generative lossy compression combines a rate-limited representation with a stochastic decoder that preserves source-dependent information while generating unresolved detail. We ask what remains reusable when a rate-distortion-perception (RDP) system selected for one operating point is transferred to a prescribed conditional-generation task. We distinguish the single-letter RDP factorization from its block-code implementation and compare Full Redesign with three increasingly restrictive transfer strategies. Renderer-Only Transfer retains only the renderer and redesigns semantic steering. Representation-Induced Transfer additionally retains the semantic latent law induced by the original representation. Full-Model Transfer retains a compatible RDP code, marginalizing over the task conditional law to form its semantic encoder. For finite alphabets, we characterize Renderer-Only Transfer's exact compression-common-randomness rate region, renderer-hull controllability condition, and compression-rate penalty relative to Full Redesign. Under unlimited common randomness, this penalty is the minimum residual semantic information $I(S;U|X)$ forced by the inherited renderer. Representation-Induced Transfer is exact if and only if the semantic condition depends on the source only through the recurrent-class label $C$ of the end-to-end RDP test channel. Every compatible RDP code reused under Full-Model Transfer preserves $C$ and supports every task satisfying $X-C-S$. Any additionally transferable within-class semantic dependence must satisfy $I(S;X|C)\le R_0-H(C)$, where $R_0$ is the inherited compression rate. The bound is exact when $R_0=H(C)$. A scalar Gaussian specialization yields a renderer-noise controllability threshold, a closed-form transfer penalty, and examples of identical Gaussian RDP test channels with different Renderer-Only Transfer capabilities.

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
authors: Mohammad Abolnejadian; Matthew Brehmer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD-<sitting>.txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use <parliament>-<session>-<number> (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. title: Grounding Intelligent Drilling Agents: A Knowledge Graph Over a Governed Drilling Data Layer for Verifiable Agentic Workflows
authors: J. Cao; L. Bianchi; L. P. Bianchini; A. Ciuca; V. Gibilterra; G. Sinibaldi; A. Livincovs; T. Yu; R. B. Muhammad
venue: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract Drilling knowledge is fragmented across daily drilling reports (DDRs), digital report repository software and WITSML exports, and project-scoped silos in which well names are free-text strings rather than linked entities. As operators begin to deploy intelligent Drilling Agents, the binding constraint is no longer model capability but context: in a safety-critical domain, an unconstrained agent will produce confident, physically impossible recommendations. This paper presents a working architecture in which a knowledge graph (KG) over a governed data layer supplies the Drilling Agent with connected, semantically rich, queryable context, and a deliberately engineered harness — not the model — makes the resulting workflows reliable, grounded, and measurable. We define a cross-operator drilling ontology aligned to OSDU and Energistics WITSML, governed under a Core/Extension/Custom model so that operator-specific fields are never silently dropped. Storage is co-located in a single database engine: relational tables act as the canonical source of truth, an in-database Apache AGE property-graph mirror carries identity, edges, and relationships, and co-located vector and time-series stores extend the same engine to free-text and high-rate channels. A process-once, serve-many pipeline parses heterogeneous exports with parse-coverage telemetry and tolerant entity resolution. Agents reach the layer only through governed tool interfaces that expose logical asset identifiers. The harness wraps agents with bounded roles, typed inter-agent contracts, schema-validated inputs and outputs, an evidence and confidence hierarchy, physics-range enforcement, human-in-the-loop gates on low-reversibility actions, and a deterministic controller whose changes are admitted only after automated evaluation. On a five-well example dataset (daily drilling report exports), the pipeline materialized some 6,450 governed core entities across 15 entity types — including 806 non-productive time (NPT) events, 2,829 coded operational activities, 1,360 survey stations, 531 bottomhole assembly (BHA) components, 393 mud checks, and 39 BHA runs — with zero load failures and column-level mapping telemetry for every source field, and mirrored them into a knowledge graph enriched with computed cross-well relationships. Offset-well discovery, shared-equipment lookup, and NPT and bit-run analytics that previously took hours of manual cross-referencing now return in interactive time: seconds for the governed queries, one to two minutes for complete agent responses. Physics-range enforcement and the evidence hierarchy block out-of-envelope recommendations at the tool boundary, and every answer returns an explicit evidence chain over schema-validated, logged tool calls.

title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
authors: Alireza Mansourkhaki; Kambiz Talebi; Jahangir Yadollahi Farsi
venue: International Journal of Innovation Management and Organizational Behavior (IJIMOB)
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. Human capital and organizational learning played a central role in sustaining and institutionalizing the strategic pivot. Conclusion: Strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group represents a multidimensional organizational response to environmental uncertainty rather than an isolated managerial decision. Successful pivots require alignment among market responses, structural transformation, technological innovation, operational resilience, and organizational learning. The proposed conceptual model can help managers recognize environmental signals, coordinate adaptive actions, and strengthen organizational resilience and long-term competitiveness.
